tropes.name: Forced Team-Up
tropes.definition: Circumstances compel two characters who wouldn't normally work together to collaborate against their initial preference.

tropes.name: Rivals to Allies
tropes.definition: Characters who begin in competition or conflict develop genuine mutual respect and become allies through shared adversity.

tropes.name: Found Family
tropes.definition: Characters build a familial, non-romantic bond with people who are not biologically related, often replacing or supplementing absent family.

tropes.name: Found Siblings
tropes.definition: Two characters develop a sibling-like bond -- protective, teasing, unconditionally loyal -- despite no biological relation.

tropes.name: Odd Couple
tropes.definition: Characters with contrasting personalities, values, or methods are forced into cooperation, and their differences become a source of both friction and strength.

tropes.name: Secret Identity
tropes.definition: One character conceals a crucial truth about themselves (an identity, power, or origin) from the other, creating tension around eventual discovery.

tropes.name: Hurt/Comfort
tropes.definition: One character is physically or emotionally wounded, and the other provides platonic care, support, or protection.

tropes.name: Protective Streak
tropes.definition: One character displays strong instinctive protectiveness over the other, often before real trust has been established.

tropes.name: Mentor and Student
tropes.definition: A more experienced character guides a less experienced one, with the dynamic evolving as the student grows into their own capability.

tropes.name: Miscommunication
tropes.definition: Conflict or delay is driven primarily by characters misunderstanding each other's words, actions, or intentions.

tropes.name: Role Reversal
tropes.definition: Characters swap typical dynamics of power, dependence, or expertise, forcing new interaction patterns.

tropes.name: Betrayal and Reconciliation
tropes.definition: Trust between characters is broken by a real or perceived betrayal, and the story tracks whether and how it's repaired.

tropes.name: Fish Out of Water
tropes.definition: A character finds themselves operating by unfamiliar rules, culture, or context (often the driving premise of a crossover), and must adapt.

tropes.name: Second Chance
tropes.definition: Characters with a lapsed or damaged relationship are given renewed opportunity to reconnect.

tropes.name: Loyalty Tested
tropes.definition: A character faces a situation that directly tests where their loyalty truly lies, often between competing obligations.

tropes.name: Unlikely Alliance
tropes.definition: Characters from fundamentally different worlds, value systems, or factions set aside their differences to cooperate toward a shared goal.
